Methyl ester content 96.5 to 99.5 wt% (specification minimum 96.5 wt%), desired resolution 0.2 wt%
Residual methanol 0.05 to 0.5 wt% at MP-2
Water 200 to 2000 ppm depending on the point; specification limit 500 ppm in the final product
Free and total glycerol of interest but secondary
MP-1 outlet of reactor R-202 (line DN80); MP-2 outlet of wash column C-301 (line DN50); MP-3 outlet of dryer D-401 (line DN50)
Throughput 12 m³/h; MP-1 60 to 65 °C, 3 barg; MP-2 40 to 50 °C, 2 barg; MP-3 80 to 90 °C, 1.5 barg

status_reason: Material, target quantities and measurement points are stated, so a provisional assessment is possible. The accuracy targets, fiber run and probe certification are not yet shown to be achievable, so there is no in-line decision yet.
answer: Test MIR ATR first, at MP-3, with a Zone 1 certified ATR probe on a PIR fiber, because the only water-in-oil ATR example in the sources uses this method; compare it with NIR on the same samples. The accuracy targets, the 45 to 60 m fiber run and the probe certification are not yet shown to be achievable, so this is a lab-first test and not a decision.

inline.headline: Test MIR ATR on a PIR fiber probe for ester content, methanol and water at MP-3 first, against NIR on the same samples
inline.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 or diamond tip sealed in a PEEK shaft, Zone 1 certified (certification unverified)
inline.install: Online at MP-3 (dryer D-401 outlet, DN50) first, where retained samples exist; MP-1 and MP-2 after
inline.fiber: PIR (polycrystalline) mid-IR fiber to the analyzer house, 45 m (MP-2, MP-3) to 60 m (MP-1)
inline.test_against: NIR fiber probe on the same validation samples
inline.not_final_because: No source gives accuracy for MIR ATR in this matrix; the water example covers 0.1 to 2.0 % water in petroleum oil with no detection limit; the 45 to 60 m PIR run, the Zone 1 probe and the turbid MP-2 stream are unverified.

problems.text: The only water example is petroleum oil with 0.1 to 2.0 % water measured by MIR ATR. The client's water targets are 200 to 2000 ppm with 50 ppm accuracy, so the example does not show MIR ATR at the ppm range.

The accuracy targets (ester within 0.3 wt%, methanol within 0.05 wt%, water within 50 ppm against the laboratory) are not supported by any source; the water example gives no detection limit and no process conditions.

The spectrometer is planned in the analyzer house 45 to 60 m away, but no fiber is installed. The mid-IR fiber ranges are given without any run length, and hollow waveguides couple poorly to FTIR while PIR fibers couple better in ATR probes.

All probes and housings at the line must be Zone 1 certified. No certified ATR probe appears in the sources, and line-mounted spectrometers would need Zone 1 housings, so the analyzer house is the only Zone 1-free option shown.

The MP-2 stream can be turbid from entrained water droplets until drying. UV-ATR is suggested for turbid media, and heterogeneous samples need all methods to see the same spot, so the MP-2 probe geometry is not settled.

The document conflicts with itself: MP-2 methanol is 0.1 to 0.5 wt% in the MP-2 description but 0.05 to 0.5 wt% in the targets section, and MP-2 water is 500 to 2000 ppm in one place and 200 to 2000 ppm in another. The calibration ranges must be fixed first.

methods.why: ATR probes measure water in oil at a distance over a mid-IR fiber, and MIR gives well-defined absorption peaks; the water example is the only application of this kind in the sources, so it is the method to test first.

NIR is the most common online fiber-probe method and suits remote fiber probes, but its broad overlapping bands need chemometrics, and a bioprocess example reports possible lack of sensitivity below 0.1 %.

Raman is complementary to MIR and needs special probes; the pharmaceutical example used 785 nm excitation, with the Raman shift in cm-1 as the axis. Weak signals and fluorescence in many organic compounds make it a fallback only.
Most chemicals do not fluoresce, and the fused approach was limited to samples with at least one fluorescent component; no fluorescent marker for these targets appears in the sources.
UV-ATR suits opaque or turbid media, but overlapping signals in real mixtures require chemometrics, and no source links UV-Vis to ester, methanol or water in this matrix.

questions.q: Which methanol range is correct for MP-2, 0.05 to 0.5 wt% or 0.1 to 0.5 wt%, and which water range applies, 200 or 500 ppm lower limit?
questions.why: The document states both values, so the calibration range cannot be set.

questions.q: Can you provide retained samples with laboratory reference values for MP-1 and MP-2, not only for MP-3?
questions.why: Only MP-3 has about 900 retained samples, so a first model cannot be built at the other points without reference samples.

questions.q: Is a Zone 1 certified ATR probe with a mid-IR fiber already available, and which ATEX marking must it carry?
questions.why: All probes at the line must be Zone 1 certified and all equipment must carry ATEX marking; this decides the probe choice.

questions.q: What is the maximum permitted fiber run from MP-3 to the analyzer house, and is a 45 m mid-IR fiber run acceptable?
questions.why: No fiber is installed and no mid-IR run length is given in the sources.

questions.q: Can a sample from MP-2 with entrained water droplets be supplied for a turbidity test?
questions.why: Turbidity at MP-2 can disturb the measurement and decides the probe geometry.

technical.spectral_window: MIR 3 to 17 µm for the PIR fiber (S02-6-fibers; 3 to 16 µm in S02-8-pir). The water example covers 4000 to 2000 cm-1, i.e. 2.5 to 5 µm (REF-units). The ester carbonyl near 1740 cm-1 (about 5.7 µm) is cited for fat in S04-3-design and must be tested for ester content.
technical.probe: ATR probe with ZrO2 or diamond tip sealed in a PEEK shaft and PEEK tubing (P:S02-p13-1); PIR fiber couples better than hollow waveguides in ATR probes (S02-9-hwg); Zone 1 certified (P:DOC-p4-1). Tip compatibility with methanol, KOH and glycerol: unknown – ask.
technical.fiber: PIR mid-IR fiber from the analyzer house, 45 m (MP-2, MP-3) to 60 m (MP-1) (P:DOC-p6-1); transmission at that length unknown – ask. No fiber is installed; existing cable trays can carry fiber (P:DOC-p6-1).
technical.process_conditions: MP-1 60 to 65 °C, 3 barg, 12 m³/h, DN80 stainless 1.4571; MP-2 40 to 50 °C, 2 barg, DN50; MP-3 80 to 90 °C, 1.5 barg, DN50 (P:DOC-p4-1). ATEX Zone 1 at all points. Cleaning with hot water at 80 °C during shutdowns, no CIP chemicals; wetted materials must be compatible with methanol, KOH traces and glycerol (P:DOC-p8-1).
technical.sampling: Start at MP-3, then MP-1 and MP-2; a new value at least every 2 minutes per point (P:DOC-p8-1). Laboratory reference runs about 6 samples per day per point with 2-hour turnaround (P:DOC-p7-1); today's off-line measurement is every 4 hours (P:DOC-p2-1).
technical.reference_method: Ester by GC per EN 14103; methanol by headspace GC per EN 14110; water by coulometric Karl Fischer per EN ISO 12937 (P:DOC-p7-1). These are independent laboratory analyses, not the instrument calibration.
technical.calibration: First model from MP-3 retained samples, about 900 over 18 months, stored at room temperature in closed glass bottles (P:DOC-p7-1). Ranges: ester 96.5 to 99.5 wt% at 0.2 wt% resolution, methanol 0.05 to 0.5 wt% at MP-2, water 200 to 2000 ppm (P:DOC-p5-1). Number of calibration samples: unknown – ask.

experiment.objective: Find out whether MIR ATR on a PIR fiber sees ester content, methanol and water in the client's matrix, and whether it beats NIR on the same samples.
steps: Select a sample set from the MP-3 retained samples (about 900) and the laboratory list of reference values, covering the ester, methanol and water ranges; check whether closed-bottle storage at room temperature changes the water content before using them as reference (P:DOC-p7-1, P:DOC-p13-1).
Record MIR ATR spectra on the existing plant FTIR with diamond ATR (P:DOC-p6-1, not process-rated) over 4000 to 2000 cm-1 and look for the ester carbonyl and water bands (P:S02-p13-1, S04-3-design).
Record NIR spectra of the same samples with a silica fiber diffuse-reflection or transmission probe to build the NIR comparison (S02-11-refl, S01-10-nir).

Build PLS models per method on a calibration set and test on a held-out validation set against EN 14103, EN 14110 and EN ISO 12937; do not derive accuracy from a few spectra (S01-5-chemometrics, P:DOC-p7-1).
Test MIR ATR + NIR by low-level fusion of synchronised spectra on the same validation set; keep the fusion only if it beats the best single method (S01-9-fusion, S01-8-same-spot).
Bench-test probe materials against hot water at 80 °C and against methanol, KOH traces and glycerol; test the MP-2 turbid sample with water droplets (P:DOC-p8-1, P:DOC-p3-2).
Ask the supplier for mid-IR fiber transmission over 45 to 60 m and for Zone 1 certified ATR probe options (P:DOC-p9-1, P:DOC-p4-1).
experiment.go_no_go: Go only if, on held-out laboratory samples, the method meets ester within 0.3 wt%, methanol within 0.05 wt% and water within 50 ppm against the laboratory reference, gives a value at least every 2 minutes, the probe is Zone 1 certified and the fiber transmits over 45 to 60 m. These criteria come from the client.

pathway.key_features: Candidate bands: ester carbonyl near 1740 cm-1 (cited for fat in S04-3-design; to be tested for ester content) and the water absorbance region 4000 to 2000 cm-1 (P:S02-p13-1). No client spectra are supplied, so no key features can be confirmed yet.
pathway.path_reason: The method must first be shown on the client's samples; no spectra and no accuracy data exist yet.

multispectral.why: MIR gives well-defined peaks while NIR bands are broad and overlapping (S01-5-chemometrics), so the pair may separate features one method blurs; NIR also reaches further into the stream (S01-10-nir). Mixed-phase media may need more than one method (S01-7-synergy).
multispectral.test: On the same validation samples, compare MIR ATR alone, NIR alone and fused MIR + NIR PLS models for ester, methanol and water against EN 14103, EN 14110 and EN ISO 12937; the combination counts only if it beats the best single method. A combined same-spot probe is needed only if MP-2 proves heterogeneous, since no combined MIR + NIR probe is shown in the sources.

assumptions: The MIR fiber to the analyzer house is PIR; no source confirms its length or transmission.
The plant laboratory FTIR is not process-rated and is used only for the spectral survey (P:DOC-p6-1).
Probe certification and fiber transmission at 45 to 60 m are unverified.
The MP-2 methanol and water ranges are unresolved between sections of the document.
One multiplexed spectrometer for all three points is not assumed; the supplier is asked.
